title: Refine paired parameters and derive the fixed-exponent supremum
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The existing h=50 paired parameters support a minimum margin of 1.7418148416e-18. This parameter-only refinement retains their declared bit and complex exponent savings and supplies the larger strict target kappa=1.7523184e-18, about 0.603% above that existing margin (1.014% above the rounded 2^-59 headline).

Use the exact rational choices beta=99999912384/10^11, epsilon=1999999999999/10^13, delta=10^-14 and C1=2, with a=296/10^11, s=1/10^11, c=beta*a, lambda=1-(1+beta)*a^2/2 and lambda-prime=1-beta*a^2. Their minimum margin is 1.7523184646864326407676563456e-18, strictly above the claimed target.

The accompanying audit derives the exact supremum for the fixed declared a,s,C1 and revised inequalities: G*=q*/(5+4*q*), with q* the smaller positive root of a*q^2-(s+a^2)*q+a^2*s=0. It supplies an upper bound and an approaching feasible family, with all other constraints checked. This does not claim optimality for other exponent estimates, circuits or algorithms.

The contribution adds an independent rational checker, an integrated certificate, a dependency ledger, an independent patch against the pinned manuscript, and regression tests. The paired circuits, nonadjacent routing, stopped-guard and tight-Gaussian interfaces are inherited. The separate 2^-58 role-budget target is explicitly unachieved. The full multiplication theorem remains assumed; there is no practical speedup or global priority claim.

Developed by Aurel Prosz (Paureel) with substantial OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assistance; original construction and manuscript attribution retained. Please review the constrained supremum proof and the parameter dependency argument independently.

## Validation

- Full make verify passed locally with Python 3.12.14: 103 tests, including 18 refinement tests, and all 17 independent patch application checks.
- All 30 strict parameter slacks and all seven margins match the existing verifier exactly; the inherited paired coefficients, frames, guard constants and pinned source hashes were rechecked.
- Separate tests derive the seven cost powers from the manuscript's d,K,ell,alpha factors, exercise failure boundaries and the strict absorption gap, and check the exact supremum balancing identity and feasible approaching family.
- Certificates and patches regenerate without changes; upstream/, existing notes, PDFs and license are unchanged.
- A disposable flattened manuscript syntax preview compiled successfully. Only the preview omitted pdfTeX-specific metadata and used bibliography labels instead of external BibTeX files; those adjustments are excluded from the patch.

Numerical checks and successful compilation do not constitute a formal verification of the complete multiplication-machine theorem.

title: Preserve aligned pairing and its conditional 17*2^-63 witness
body:
This preserves the aligned-pair refinement of the historical `2^-59` construction against current upstream. Its certificate, proof packet and original feature code are unchanged. The README places its standalone conditional target alongside the newer, stronger community construction, with the remaining independent review obligations explicit.

Aligning the global pair groups between common-point circuits removes 14,944 additions at `h=50`. Under the same retained analytic recipe and upstream theorem, the exact bit saving supports a conditional target of **κ = 17·2⁻⁶³**, 6.25% above the earlier paired witness target `2^-59`.

For common point `i`, put its global pair partner `i ^ 1` last in the local point order and leave all other complete pairs together. Relabel local inputs and outputs consistently. The original 49-point paired circuit is unchanged; the existing fixed-pair-star sharing now identifies more equal sums across common-point groups.

- Additions: `450394 → 435450`; side roles: `509194 → 494250`; all `58800` partial outputs retained.
- Exact counts: `W=394839648000000`, `s=49354954232864000000`, unchanged deficit `D=1767136000000`, and `eta_b=23/642375000`.
- Bit saving: `a_b=305/10^11`, using the existing rational logarithm enclosure. With the retained complex motif, stopped guard and Gaussian recipe, all 30 strict constraints and seven margins pass. The exact minimum is `G=739738521/400000000000000000000000000 > 17*2^-63`.

Includes an exact certificate, a short proof note/PDF, a construction and dependency audit, and an independent patch against the unchanged pinned upstream source. The previous paired witness and its generated patch remain reproducible. This changes the graph supplying the bit exponent and complements #1's parameter refinement.

Current-base validation: full `make verify` passes **224 tests and 21 independent patch checks** under Linux/GCC. Every upstream validation target is retained, and all regenerated certificates and patches match their Git blobs exactly. New coverage includes a full-size expansion of the actual global DAG in 1,024-input chunks, independent of compressed provenance; small dense support checks; both frame directions; and dirty-scratch/bank-exchange checks. The proof note and complete patched manuscript compile.

The complete upstream multiplication theorem and retained analytic interfaces remain assumptions. No family optimum, dyadic `2^-58` target or practical speedup is claimed.

Focused mathematical review: the [review packet](https://github.com/Bortlesboat/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1c200af99d348de496d78274de3584339dcf02e3/docs/research/aligned-paired-review.md) ([three-page PDF](https://github.com/Bortlesboat/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1c200af99d348de496d78274de3584339dcf02e3/artifacts/aligned-paired-review.pdf)) separates the finite claim from the conditional running-time result, identifies the rank/restoration, fixed-tape recurrence and downstream proof obligations, and gives reproduction commands. External expert assessment of those obligations is requested and remains pending.

title: Compress the complex network for a conditional 59/10^11 > 2^-31 bound
body:
## Summary

After compact control (`83/10^12`), the binding motif is the complex network, which still uses the original side wires: one per ordered neighbor pair, **3,693,800 per invocation** at `h=25`. This PR computes the same side correction with shared sums in **108,195 reversible roles**, raising the certified complex saving from `418/10^12` to **`14/10^9`** (33.5x). The paired bit network then becomes the only binding motif, and the unchanged compact-control recurrence and assembly give the conditional witness

**`kappa = 59/10^11 > 2^-31`**, a factor `590/83 ≈ 7.11` above `83/10^12`.

Bit network, compact-control movement/reservations/repair, generalized guard, Gaussian setup and assembly are all unchanged. This builds directly on `6e56487` and does not overlap #1 or #2 (both refine the bit network on the earlier line; an improved bit saving would compose with this change).

## Construction

- **Disjoint triples** (weight `+1/2`): recursive halving of the 25 ordered points computes triple sums avoiding up to three points; each target receives six pieces.
- **Intersection-two triples** (weight `-1/2`): prefix/suffix sums of each pair star around the excluded third point.
- **Roles and schedule**: the bit network's `c+q` reversible compiler and transparent schedule `L,-J,L^-1,-R,V,G,R,L,J,L^-1,G^-1,V^-1`, with signs, restore arbitrary scratch.
- **Binary frames**: inputs get `<t_T>`, disjoint-sum nodes the coordinate space of their covered points, pair-star nodes the (orthonormal) span of their `t_abu`. The one new obstruction: an injected disjoint piece covering every point outside its target has injection residual `<e_a+e_b, e_b+e_c>`, which is nondegenerate but alternating (no orthonormal basis), and no relabeling avoids it. Pieces are therefore injected only when they leave an outside point `y` uncovered, so `e_y` lies in the residual. The reversed stage uses orthogonal complements, whose residuals equal forward ones.

Counts: `W_c = 1,741,801,270,000`, `s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c`, `eta_c = 28/205,789,375`. Total gates `5.41e12 <= 12 W_c`, coefficients in `{0,±1,±1/2}`, so `E = 64(W_c+m+1)^3` and the generalized guard apply with the new constants.

Witness: `epsilon = 19999/100000`, `c = 999/1000` (with `sigma < tau`, the old `c = 1/5` would make `g2` binding), `lambda = 1-2958/10^12`, `lambda' = 1-2956/10^12`; minimum margin `g3 = 14779261/(25·10^15)`, gap `29261/(25·10^15)`. Scoped next ceiling: with the published bit network and `epsilon < 1/5`, `kappa < a_b/5 < 2^-30`.

## Artifacts

- Proof note: `notes/complex-circuit-note.tex` / `artifacts/complex-circuit-note.pdf`
- Summary: `docs/research/complex-circuit.md`
- Certificate: `certificates/complex-network.json` (`scripts/complex_network.py`)
- Combined patch on top of compact control: `patches/complex-circuit-31.patch` (`scripts/make_complex_circuit_patch.py`)
- README headline, status page, reproducibility notes and Makefile targets (`make complex-note`)

## Validation

- [x] `make verify` passes: all generators, 173 tests, all 18 patch-application checks; existing certificates and patches regenerate byte-identically.
- [x] Full-size exact checks at `h=25`: all 3,693,800 nonzero side coefficients and every zero; all 82,895 labels (nondegenerate, with odd-vector residuals on 188,790 inclusions); all 108,195 compiled roles in both stage directions.
- [x] Small complete cases (`h=8..12`): dirty-scratch forward and inverse invocations, the signed exchange, and every input basis vector through an `h=8` invocation; binary label algebra checked against brute-force enumeration; the alternating-plane obstruction reproduced; witness rejected with `c=1/5`, `epsilon=1/5`, or the old complex saving.
- [x] The patched manuscript compiles with Tectonic with no unresolved references.

These checks support the written argument; they are not a formal verification. The upstream theorem remains assumed and the new binary-frame transfer has not been independently reviewed. **Review focus:** Lemma `complex-piece-residual` and the inverse-stage frame assignment (§3.4 of the note).

Contributed by eumemic, prepared with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

title: Faster Gaussian resampling for a conditional 1479/10^12 > 2^-30 bound
body:
Builds on #3 (compressed complex network); until #3 merges, this diff includes its two commits. The new commit is d3d370c.

## Summary

With the compressed complex network, the binding constraint was the Gaussian resampling step. Its line maps cost `O(t p^(3/2+delta) alpha)`, which forces `epsilon < 1/5` and caps `kappa < a_b/5`. This PR removes that cap:

- **Chirped correlations.** `(sigma a - b)^2 = sigma theta a^2 + sigma (a-b)^2 - theta b^2` turns each block of Gaussian sums into one correlation. The established `O(N log N)` multiplier evaluates it in `O(p^(1+delta))` per output, independent of `alpha`. This covers both `S'` and the correction `E = N - I`, with the same truncation windows and error interfaces as HvdH Lemmas 4.9 and 4.11.
- **Powers of the correction.** A potential argument (`Phi(j) = sigma(beta_j^2 + 1/4)/theta`) gives `||E^n|| <= exp(pi alpha^2 (1/(4 theta)+1/2)) (2.01 exp(-pi alpha^2 sigma))^n`. The Neumann series of HvdH Lemma 4.12 then needs at most `ceil((p+1)/(4 alpha^2) + 1/theta)` terms instead of `ceil(p/(alpha^2 theta))`. Its error analysis is otherwise unchanged.
- **New width.** `alpha = floor(sqrt(b/(8d)))` keeps `gamma <= b/4`, the bound used by the retained rounding argument, and gives `alpha^2 theta_i >= 1` and Neumann counts `<= 30d`. The Gaussian row becomes `O(d^2 p^delta)` per bit, with power `2 eps + delta`, so `epsilon` may approach `1/2`.
- **Parameters.** `epsilon = 49999/100000`, `c = 9999/10000`, `beta = 19/25`. The guard needs `beta > 3/4` at this epsilon, and the leaf needs `(1-beta) a_c > 1 - lambda'`. Both hold only with the compressed complex saving `14/10^9`.

The exact conditional witness is **κ = 1479/10¹² ≈ 1.479e-9 > 2⁻³⁰**. That is 1479/590 ≈ 2.51 times `59/10^11` and about 17.8 times `83/10^12`. The new scoped ceiling for these networks is `kappa < a_b/2 < 2^-29` (`g2, g3, g4 <= a_b min(eps, 1-eps)`).

The bit and complex networks, compact-control movement, reservation, repair and guard are unchanged. The patch modifies the one-dimensional resampling lemma, adds a subsection with the two new lemmas and a corollary, and updates the tensor interface time, Gaussian width, prime checks, cost row, `g5` and parameters.

## Verification

- `make verify`: 182 tests pass, all 19 patch checks apply, certificates regenerate exactly (2m47s locally).
- `scripts/fast_gaussian.py` checks the witness and guard exactly. It also checks the step identity `c(j,h) - Phi(j+h) + Phi(j) = sigma h^2 + (sigma/theta) w(2y-w) >= sigma h^2` on several `(s,t)`, and the Neumann counts.
- `tests/test_fast_gaussian.py` covers:
  - the chirp identity, exactly;
  - explicit `E^n` against both bounds, at 160 decimal digits;
  - chirped blocks against direct Gaussian sums;
  - negative cases: `eps = 1/2`, `beta` too small or too large, the old complex saving;
  - the patch text.
- The full patched manuscript compiles with Tectonic with no undefined references. The 6-page note builds with `make fast-gaussian-note`.

This remains conditional on the pinned upstream interfaces, the compact-control construction, the compressed complex network and the written arguments. It is not independent review or formal verification.

Contributed by eumemic, with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

title: Aligned bit circuit with cheaper centers for a conditional 1624/10^12 bound
body:
Builds on #5 (fast Gaussian resampling), which builds on #3. Until those merge, this diff includes their commits; the new commit is 5015011.

## Summary

With fast resampling, `kappa < a_b/2` (`g2, g3, g4 <= a_b min(eps, 1-eps)`), so only the bit network matters. Two changes raise its saving from `296/10^11` to **`325/10^11`**:

- **Cheaper centers.** Each center wire now takes its value from the group total `z_i = sum_{T contains i} x_T`, computed inside the side circuit. Its frame there is `D_{H_i}`, where `H_i` is the star span of dimension `h-1`; the scatter stays at `D_0`. Each center therefore loses `h-1` instead of `h` dimensions per invocation. In stage 2 the center rises to `D_1` at the scatter and falls to `D_{H_i^perp}` at the reversed total, again losing `h-1`. The deficit numerator goes from `v - 6h^2 = 4600` to `v - 6h(h-1) = 4900`.
- **Aligned side circuit.** The paired recursion uses blocks `{2k, 2k+1}` in every common-point group. Each top-level leave-one-block-out chain of a pair-star `{i, q}` runs over the blocks avoiding both `i` and `q`, so groups `i` and `q` share it, plus one group-specific triple. Side additions: 435,346, including the 50 totals. Roles per invocation, including the centers: **494,196 vs 509,244**.

New interface: `W = 394759742720000`, `s = Wm - N + 6v^2 h(h-1)`, `Wm - s = 1882384000000`, `eta_b = 49/1284490000 > (325/10^11)(11737/1000)`.

The exact conditional witness is **κ = 1624/10¹² ≈ 1.624e-9 > 2⁻³⁰**: 1624/1479 ≈ 1.10 times #5, and about 19.6 times `83/10^12`. The parameters are those of #5 except `tau`, `lambda = 1 - 32495/10^13` and `lambda' = 1 - 3249/10^12`. The minimum margin is `g3 = 162446751/10^17`.

The leaf needs `(1 - beta) a_c > 1 - lambda'` and the guard needs `beta > 3/4`. `beta = 19/25` satisfies both with the compressed complex saving, but only just: a further ~2% on `a_b` would need a sharper guard or a stronger complex saving.

## Verification

- `scripts/bit_circuit.py` at h=50 checks every partial output and total exactly, the disjointness of every addition, the common point of every node, and all 494,196 compiled roles' frames in both directions.
- `tests/test_aligned_bit_network.py` covers:
  - full checks and an exact F2 simulation of the new schedule, with dirty scratch, in both stage directions, for h = 8..14;
  - the rank `h - 1` of the star span;
  - counts, and the fact that 325/10^11 fails with the old `h^2` center loss;
  - the parameter windows and the patch text.
- `patches/aligned-bit-30.patch` applies to the pinned source, and the full patched manuscript compiles with Tectonic with no undefined references. The 3-page note is `artifacts/aligned-bit-note.pdf`.
- New components pass on their own. The full `make verify` is still running locally on a heavily loaded machine; I'll comment with the result.

This remains conditional on the pinned upstream interfaces and the stacked written arguments. It is not independent review or formal verification.

Contributed by eumemic, with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

title: Ternary five-subset networks for a conditional 373/10^11 > 2^-28 bound
body:
## Result and base

This PR targets **`main`**, based directly on `6e564879f51ae16f23d392e9e196c605f36d90df`. It supplies a conditional integer-multiplication witness

**κ = 373/10¹¹ = 3.73e-9 > 2⁻²⁸**, for `T(n) = O(n (log n)^(1-κ))` in the retained fixed finite-alphabet, fixed-tape model.

At the submission-time check, main still supplies `83/10^12`, and the strongest headline among existing PRs #1–#6 is #6's `1624/10^12`. The new witness is about **2.30 times #6**. This is an asymptotic exponent comparison, not a practical runtime claim or an unrestricted optimality claim.

## Construction

- **Ternary five-subset interchange:** use F3 payloads on the five-subsets of 28 points, with rational address labels `H = I - (2/25)J`. The coefficient identity `binom(k,2) - [k=2] = [k=5] (mod 3)` supplies the scalar identity. Retained common-pair totals have span dimension `h-2`; the transparent forward/inverse schedules restore arbitrary scratch.
- **Paired degree-three recursion and star resynthesis:** exact global support merging followed by deterministic common-four-point resynthesis saves 383,216 additions. The independently checked upper bound is 10,857,762 additions plus 983,178 output uses, hence **11,840,940 auxiliary roles per invocation**. An explicit neighbor permutation shares first/third-stage banks. The rational-frame argument and finite-alphabet transfer support `a_b = 3/400000000`.
- **Stronger complex producer:** paired triple exclusion replaces the disjoint producer in #3's binary-label interface. Full-size checks give 61,022 additions, 32,816 injected pieces and 93,838 roles; #4's bank-sharing argument then supports `a_c = 39/10^9`.
- **Composition:** retain compact controls and #5's fast Gaussian resampling. All 29 exact constraints and seven margins are strict. The minimum margin is `934813/250000000000000`, with gap `2313/250000000000000` above κ. The source patch updates the actual downstream consumers, including the integer rounding comparison for the selected epsilon.

## Review and reproducibility

- `make verify`: **188 tests pass; all 20 independent patch checks pass**.
- Complete h=28 producer regeneration checks every local coefficient, exact global support key and resynthesized boundary sum; every replacement addition has disjoint support. Hash tables use full equality checks, not probabilistic fingerprints.
- All 98,280 neighbor images are distinct and have intersection two. At h=8, all 1,156 scalar basis inputs (including dirty scratch) and both exact rational-frame directions pass. The h=28 complex circuit passes every coefficient, binary-label, injection-residual and compiled-role check.
- Negative controls reject uncompressed stars, old center losses, weaker complex saving, an invalid guard and an oversized headline exponent.
- The six-page proof note and full 89-page patched manuscript compile with pdfLaTeX; the final manuscript has no unresolved references. Certificates and patches regenerate exactly, and pinned `upstream/` remains unchanged.

Start with `docs/research/prime-field28.md`, `notes/prime-field28-construction.tex`, `artifacts/prime-field28-note.pdf`, `certificates/prime-field28.json` and `patches/prime-field28.patch`. Reproduce with `make verify` and `make prime-field-note`. The new exact checker requires a C++17 compiler, Python's standard library and about 1.2 GB memory.

**Review focus:** the retained-total forward/reverse rational-frame schedule, first/third-stage bank joins, and transfer from binary payloads to a fixed F3 alphabet. The pinned multiplication theorem, retained analytic interfaces and written extensions remain assumptions. Finite certificates and compilation are not independent mathematical review or formal verification of the full theorem.

## Dependencies and contribution attribution

Necessary files from eumemic's Claude-assisted #3 and #5 are imported unchanged from #5 commit `d3d370c34937503bd3fa63c83d505a05e8e50893`, so this PR is self-contained against main. Those files and results remain credited to their authors. Douglas Colkitt's framework, Bortlesboat's aligned pairing (#2), dleen's retained totals and stage sharing (#4), and eumemic's cheaper centers (#6) are credited in the note and NOTICE.

The new F3 motif, paired degree-three recursion, four-point-star resynthesis, stronger paired complex producer and their composition are contributed by **Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)** with substantial **GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI Codex)** research, proof-development and implementation assistance, as identified by the contributor. This records their **first submission of this specific construction to this repository**, not worldwide priority or an OpenAI endorsement.

**Future research building on this contribution should explicitly acknowledge Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen), cite this PR and its accompanying note, and retain the preceding contributors' attribution.** This provenance statement is also included in NOTICE and the note; the repository's Apache-2.0 license remains unchanged.

title: Review conditional geometric complex-network candidate with kappa = 5.9e-10
body:
This research candidate replaces the complex motif's separate side wires with shared disjointness and intersection-two sum circuits. Geometric envelope labels and one charged binary label coordinate are intended to make the physical frame residuals nondegenerate and nonalternating. Assuming the retained upstream and compact-control interfaces, the exact parameter calculation supports `kappa = 59/10^11 = 5.9e-10`, about 7.11 times the current conditional exponent saving. This is an asymptotic exponent comparison, not a measured runtime speedup.

The candidate adds a standalone proof note, reproducible Python programs, exact JSON certificates, and a reviewer guide in `research/geometric-complex/`. The root README explains the geometry, exponent comparison, reproduction commands, attribution, and proof boundary, presenting the new candidate separately from the retained compact-control result. It is **conditional and unreviewed**. It supplies neither formal verification of the multiplication theorem nor a combined manuscript integration patch; the existing published witnesses remain unchanged.

### Review requested

- Reversible role allocation and cancellation with arbitrary initial scratch, including the reverse schedule and three tensor stages.
- Every geometric residual, especially output/cleanup boundaries and complemented reverse frames; whether the extra label coordinate is fully charged.
- Phase factorization modulo four, common-frame telescoping, and the permitted complex-network operator.
- Full wire/rank accounting, precision guard, and use of the retained complete-layer recurrence and downstream analytic interfaces.

### Validation

- Exact candidate verification: full-size circuit supports and 1,514,542 nested role incidences; small scalar basis tests including dirty scratch; explicit rejection of the invalid construction without the additional coordinate; exact guard and assembly inequalities.
- Physical audit: all data, center, and side paths across three tensor stages and both orientations at ground sizes six and seven; 687,360 exhaustive active-factor address phase comparisons. These are finite checks, not exhaustive enumeration of the full size-25 tensor address space.
- Bounded screen of 441 unequal-factor bit configurations: no better candidate within the stated search family/range.
- Existing `make verify`: all 163 tests and 17 manuscript patch applicability checks passed.
- Current standalone LaTeX source compiled successfully with the native editor compiler.

Reproduction commands and inherited assumptions are documented in `research/geometric-complex/README.md`. The baseline is `6e564879f51ae16f23d392e9e196c605f36d90df`, pinning upstream `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`.

This work used substantial assistance from OpenAI Codex at Rohan Arun's request. Prior work and repository constructions are attributed in the note and reviewer guide. No claim of global novelty, global optimality, or an established new multiplication record is made.

### Completed independent rerun

Full verification was independently rerun on research commit `428bb215bb8a28a9177bc310c39586a4b21c2e22` and passed in 125.045 seconds on 2026-10-09 at 00:42:38 UTC: all 163 unit tests and 17 historical patch checks, followed by the candidate verifier, physical phase audit and bounded bit screen. No source drift occurred. This historical branch has no GitHub CI checks configured. See `research/geometric-complex/validation.json` for the exact commands and log hash. Mathematical review of the stated conditional interfaces remains requested; this is not a current record claim.

title: Refine PR #7 ternary star templates for conditional kappa = 3.8e-9
body:
This refines Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)'s ternary five-subset producer in #7, pinned at `6725c6a17b17871a35353fd29157f4ed851bc114`. A different greedy tie break, comparison of three candidate circuits, and deletion of unused ancestors save **170,400 additional addition nodes** in the four-point stars. Auxiliary roles per invocation fall from **11,840,940 to 11,670,540**.

Under #7's retained general interfaces, the exact witness becomes **kappa = 19/5,000,000,000 = 3.8e-9 > 2^-28**, approximately **1.88% above #7's 3.73e-9 headline**. This is a modest circuit refinement and an asymptotic exponent comparison, not a runtime benchmark or a global optimality claim.

title: Auxiliary source frames for a conditional kappa = 7699/10^10 > 2^-21 bound
body:
## Summary

This builds on #10 (icekylinx), which consumes Zhihao Chen's (jacklightChen) ternary producers from #7 unchanged. It reaches

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad \kappa=\frac{7699}{10^{10}}\approx 7.70\times10^{-7}>2^{-21},
$$

which is **6.26×** #10's `6149999/(5·10^13) > 2^-23`. No scalar circuit, label, producer or analytic interface changes. Only two finite choices change.

**1. Auxiliary source frames (interchange network).** The transfer needs only `M_sink(ρ(w)) − M_source(w) = I` for every role. An auxiliary role (`ρ(w)=w`) may therefore start in any fixed frame `M` if it ends in `I+M`. The scalar network restores its arbitrary logical value, and the physical output is `Φ_{I+M}Φ_{−M}f = Φ_I f`. This is the same mechanism that the data sources already use with `−P_{U_a}`.

At stage two every auxiliary role, including the central roles, first meets `D_0 = B⊗F⊗Q` (dimension `h²−h = 756`) and last meets `D_1 = A⊗F⊗Q` (dimension `h² = 784`). Starting these roles at `P_{D_0}` changes their edges as follows:

| edge | #10 | here |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| entrance | rank 756, all singleton calls | rank 0 |
| interior climb | 28 | 28 |
| exit | rank 21168 (784-wide corner block + 20384 block) | rank 21924 (28 singleton pivots + one 21896 block) |

The new exit `I + P_{D_0} − P_{D_1}` is the orthogonal projector onto `D_0 ⊥ D_1^⊥`. A generic member of #10's basis family `S = T(I_F⊗K)` puts its `h×h` corner in general position (new Lemma `lem:source-frame-basis`). #10's large-projector factorization then compiles it as `h` singleton interchanges and one contiguous interchange. The rank sum and deficit are unchanged, but the rank moved out of singleton calls costing `ln m` each, into one block costing `ln(m/t)` per unit. **Interchange saving: `246/10^9 → 154/10^8`.**

Without nonzero auxiliary sources, every stage-two role is forced to carry about `h(h−1)` singleton rank by its gate labels, which caps #7's network near 1.8× #10 under #10's model. The source frame removes exactly that rank.

**2. A third whole-residual complex class.** The stage-three data entrances (rank `(h²−1)(h−1) = 21141`, `2v_c³` copies) become whole-residual children. Since `2·21141 > q = m+6h`, #10's dependency-path guard still sees at most one selected class per path. Its path moment is `0.9620 < 0.999`, with the same `ρ = 6/5` and `C_1`. **Complex saving: `7/10^7 → 18/10^7`**, so `σ < τ` and the complex network does not bind.

| | #10 | here |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| interchange saving `a_b` | 246/10^9 | **154/10^8** |
| complex saving `a_c` | 7/10^7 | **18/10^7** |
| `ε` | 7999999/16000000 | 499999/10^6 |
| `κ` | 6149999/(5·10^13) | **7699/10^10** |

## Checks

- `scripts/source_frame_network.py` and `certificates/source-frame-network.json` hold the exact rational rank moments.
  - Interchange gap: `> 4.69e-10`. Complex gap: `> 3.89e-9`.
  - The extended guard and all 29 strict constraints are checked.
  - All 7 assembly margins are strict, with absorption gap `492299500001/(5·10^21)`.
- `tests/test_source_frame_network.py` uses an exact `h=5` model of the stage-two frames in #10's coordinate order.
  - The exit is an idempotent of rank `m−h`, and the total rank per role is unchanged.
  - Under a random basis from #10's family, the lower-lower pivots of the exit are exactly `h` corner pivots plus the diagonal block `(i,i)`, `h ≤ i < m−h`.
  - It also covers rank bookkeeping against #10's counts, exponent boundaries, and manuscript labels and references.
- `patches/source-frame-21.patch` from `scripts/make_source_frame_patch.py` is a combined manuscript patch with #10's interfaces plus the new sections and parameters.
  - It applies with `git apply --check`.
  - A preview of the full patched manuscript compiles with no undefined or duplicate references. The pdfTeX metadata lines are dropped for tectonic.
- `make verify` passes: all 172 unit tests and all 19 manuscript patch checks.
- The proof note `artifacts/source-frame-21-note.pdf` (source `notes/source-frame-21-note.tex`) reproduces #10's framework sections verbatim, followed by the new sections.

## Remaining levers (not used)

- Batching the stage-two data entrances (rank `729 > H/2` in the fast factor) gives about +3.5%.
- The interchange denominator is now dominated by the singleton climbs and join corners of the stage-1/3 auxiliary roles.

## Attribution and scope

The source-frame lemma, its application, the extended basis lemma, the third complex class and the new witness are by eumemic, with substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic).
- Bulk recursion, the controlled basis, mixed-width rows and the dependency-path guard are icekylinx's #10.
- The ternary five-subset network and paired producers are Zhihao Chen's (jacklightChen) #7, which this work acknowledges and cites as requested there.
- Earlier work by Douglas Colkitt, Bortlesboat, dleen and eumemic is credited in `NOTICE`.

This is a conditional, unreviewed draft. It relies on the pinned upstream theorem, the interfaces of #10 and its predecessors, and the written arguments here. The exact certificates and finite tests are not formal verification.

body:
The A5 projector corner in icekylinx's #18 basis contains a contiguous block of 21 pivots that the previous certificate charged as separate singleton swaps. Using that block, with Zhihao Chen's #21 translated frames and #23 semantic/bulk assembly, gives

$$T(n)=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad \kappa=\frac{11447067}{10^{12}}=1.1447067\times10^{-5}>2^{-17}.$$

This is about **4.159% above #23's 1.099e-5 witness** in asymptotic exponent saving. It is not a practical runtime claim.

### New geometric block

The profile changes from `47 singleton swaps + 481` to **`26 singleton swaps + 21 + 481`**. After the first scalar pivot in the prescribed 47-square null corner, the rank-one term cancels exactly on rows 1–21 and columns 25–45. Entries to the right of column i+24 vanish; each pivot at (i,i+24) is the generically nonzero product p_i ξ_(i+2). These consecutive, equally ordered pivots form one contiguous recursive interchange under the retained triangular conjugation. The old full-rank tree proof supplies the remaining pivots, and the middle block of width 481 is unchanged.

There are 2N occurrences: subtract 42N singleton children and add 2N children of width 21. Rank mass stays fixed, and the recursive child count falls by 40N. This general identity uses the existing simultaneous basis; finite samples are controls, not its proof.

### Compatible assembly

The exact bit saving is **1144733/10^11 = 11.44733e-6**, with moment gap greater than 3e-14. The physical graph, role count, dimension, weighted rank sum and maximum bit child are unchanged. Therefore #23's bit halving depth 494, wire exponent 43, complex scalar charge, semantic guard C1=1 and product reservoir p^89000 remain valid.

The complex saving stays 18e-6 and beta=1/4, giving leaf saving 13.5e-6 above the new bit saving. The #23 assembly recipe is recomputed at the new bit exponent, including every strict constraint and final margin.

### Review and validation

- Four new regression tests passed, including four exact rational corner cases, both projector signs, every stated Schur entry, and two negative controls per case.
- Both moments, all 47 strict constraints and seven margins pass. The final absorption gap exceeds 5e-13. Negative controls reject omitting the new block, the next certificate grid point, and reusing the old guard or separate exposure bounds.
- An independent parallel mathematical audit checked the general pivot proof and semantic/bulk compatibility; it separately reproduced the exact assembly.
- The four-page manuscript compiled with resolved references and no overfull boxes.
- The focused patch forward-applied to pinned #23 and reconstructed all 12 source files exactly. Inherited theorem and source hashes remain unchanged.
- Detailed evidence is in `research/a5-semantic/validation.json`.

**Full repository rerun: passed.** `make verify` exited 0 at `61f81dc`: all **180 tests**, **18 retained upstream patch checks**, and the focused 12-file PR23 patch check passed. All three retained bit producers (h25, h23, h57) and the complex histogram were freshly rebuilt and reproduced exactly. The completion time and log digest are recorded in `research/a5-semantic/validation.json`. This PR is ready for review.

This branch starts at #23 commit `661ebabc1076c9f525d7ce4967c876b203fa9827`. The main-branch diff includes its pending predecessors; the final commit isolates this geometric addition. Pinned inherited sources are preserved. The new proof explicitly incorporates the retained finite, analytic, routing, bulk, precision and tape dependencies. This is conditional mathematical work with exact executable checks, not formal verification or completed external expert review. No global-optimality claim is made.

### Attribution

The additional A5 contiguous-block observation, proof, controls and compatible witness are by **Rohan Arun with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**, including parallel reviews.

Credit **icekylinx** for #18's prescribed basis, partial swaps and producers, and #10's batching/tape interfaces; **Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)** for #21's translated frames and phase proof and #23's graph-specific semantic/bulk composition; **RaD/hipotures** for the semantic precision, routing, phase-cell inverse and bulk arguments exposed in #20; **eumemic** for #13 source frames and preceding work; and **Dominik Scholz** for #22's parameter tightening. Earlier #7/#16 work, Douglas Colkitt, OpenAI and all prior contributors remain credited. We do not claim their constructions as new.

title: Lean certificate check
body:
Change and mathematical scope
This PR inherits the dependencies of OpenAI's theorem and the Harvey–van der Hoeven results. If the dependency or dependencies are found to be invalid, this is likely invalid as written.

It adds formal and independent checks only. No bound, certificate, patch or note changes. Nothing here is a formal verification of the full multiplication theorem.

formal/lean/ (Lean 4 v4.21.0, Mathlib v4.21.0). Every theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; there is no sorry and no native_decide. It proves:

the κ = 83/10¹² certificate arithmetic: the counts, η, the exponent certificates, all 31 slacks, the margins, and 2⁻³⁴ < κ < g₃;
the exact scoped ceiling κ < U ≈ 8.3695980744·10⁻¹¹, with a negative control showing the enclosure exceeds U·(1 − 10⁻²⁴);
the guard note's depth derivation (Guard.lean), for every depth function that satisfies the note's two recursion inequalities, instantiated at the certified constants;
the paired circuit's frame algebra (Frames.lean): neighbor indicators are orthogonal under I − J/9, and spans of triples through a common point are anisotropic;
the compact-control address algebra (Movement.lean): the four-step parity identity, the later-source pass, the no-carry guard with exact packed-digit updates, and the repair permutation;
the layout's row arithmetic (Layout.lean).
formal/lean/SOURCES.md pairs every declaration with the note, upstream or certificate line it formalizes.

formal/circuit/. An independent check of the R = 509194 circuit that imports none of this repository's code. It recomputes every support from scratch: 450394 additions, all with disjoint supports; 58800 partial outputs, all exact; every target's neighbors partitioned; a common point at every node; and c + q = 509194 roles.

formal/open-prs/. The certificate arithmetic of the open PRs #3–#12 (libraries PRChecksA/B/C, 310 theorems), including #5's analytic inequalities and #10's bulk-guard Taylor bound. No certificate value is wrong. Circuit role counts are taken as given, and constructions written only in prose are not checked. #1 and #2 are superseded and were not Lean-checked. PRs opened after #12 are not covered. Findings:

#3 and #8: the "next ceiling" κ < 5.92·10⁻¹⁰ holds only with the bit exponent fixed at 1 − 296/10¹¹. The published h = 50 network supports 1 − τ = 2964/10¹², so the ceiling for that network is κ < 593/10¹². Their conclusion κ < 2⁻³⁰ is still valid.
#3: docs/research/complex-circuit.md:102 writes a_b/5 < 5.92e-10, but a_b/5 = 5.92·10⁻¹⁰ exactly, so the < should be =.
#4: its notes and abstract describe an older construction (R_aux = 365760, 1 − σ = 750/10¹¹), not the certified one (R = 90950, 1 − σ = 2970/10¹¹). The notes are invalid as written; the certificate and κ = 591/10¹² check.
#5 and #6: "g₂, g₃, g₄ ≤ a·min{ε, 1 − ε}" is false for g₄. At #5's witness, ε = 49999/100000, so g₄ = a(1 − ε) is slightly larger than a·ε. The true statement is min{g₃, g₄} ≤ a·min{ε, 1 − ε}, and both ceilings still hold.
#6: "a further 3% on a_b would close this window" holds only at the chosen β = 19/25. The guard allows smaller β, so the window closes at about 7.7%.
#5, Harvey–van der Hoeven wording. Its use of the lemmas holds: its parameters fail the literal hypothesis θ ≥ p/α⁴, but the proofs use that hypothesis only to obtain α²θ ≥ 1, which #5 assumes directly, and in one cost line, which #5 replaces. The text should:
say that θ ≥ p/α⁴ was also used to obtain α²θ ≥ 1;
add one sentence that the proofs of Lemmas 4.8, 4.9 and 4.11 use only 2 ≤ α < √p, s < t < 2^p, p ≥ 100 and the norms of Proposition 4.7(i);
correct the E map: its error bound with F = e^(πα²/4) fails once α ≥ 21. With F := 2^⌈1.14α²⌉, P = 34p still suffices.
None of these findings changes a headline κ.

Not verified:

the tape-machine level: tapes, streaming and running time;
that the algorithm meets the depth-recursion hypotheses;
the open PRs' prose constructions and circuit role counts;
the upstream theorem.
Prepared with substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

Validation
cd formal/lean && lake build builds all four libraries.
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests passes: 169 tests, 4 of them new.
test_lean_sources: every declaration is listed in SOURCES.md, every cited line still contains its quoted text, and every certificate value equals its Lean literal.
test_paired_circuit_check: the independent checker accepts the real circuit at h = 14 and rejects mutated circuits.
test_open_pr_lean: the drift tests for #3–#12, plus SHA-256 checks of the vendored PR files against their recorded head commits.
The full h = 50 circuit check (formal/circuit/check_paired.py) takes about 2 minutes and is not part of the test suite.
Finite tests check implementations and identities; the Lean proofs cover only the statements listed above.

title: Rectangular geometry for conditional κ = 1.2260937e-5 > 2^-17
body:

$$T(n)=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad \kappa=\frac{12260937}{10^{12}}=1.2260937\times10^{-5}>2^{-17}.$$

This is about **2.4127% above #27's 1.19720853e-5 witness** in asymptotic exponent saving. It is not a practical runtime comparison.

The prescribed basis construction extends from (25,23,57) to (28,27,57), with an explicit compatible system of partial permutations and two A5 incidence trees. The written A1 argument tracks the actual coefficient groups and nonzero pivot factors. The A3 proof cancels a rank-56 perturbation and establishes the full null-corner rank using free second rows and penultimate inverse columns in disjoint prescription intervals. Generic nonproportionality supplies the necessary nonzero diagonal entries.

The changed bit dimensions require a new product row stock: bit halving depth **553**, bit wire exponent **44**, complex depth **544**, and complex wire exponent **41**. title: Two-stage controlled corners for a conditional 15536/10^9 > 2^-16 bound
body:
The unequal two-stage construction gives the conditional final bound

**T(n)=O(n (log n)^(1−κ)), κ=15536/10^9=1.5536×10^-5 > 2^-16.**

Paureel's two-stage topology saves a tensor factor but requires a paid rank-one endpoint correction. Combining it with icekylinx's PR24 retained-total producers and a compatible controlled inner basis at dimensions **(55,53)** gives bit saving **15537/10^9**. Both auxiliary small corners and every local projector profile use the same rational basis. A supplied exact modular full-rank witness lifts to a rational nonvanishing witness for the data corner; the finite-product argument imposes all physical conditions simultaneously. No independently selected per-edge bases, uncharged gathers, or omitted correction calls are used.

The actual rebuilt producers have **R53=580787** and **R55=652589**, including their retained centers. The complete physical list has **m=2915, W=31753659079, s=92561585391935**, with deficit **330823350**. title: Exact data-corner certificates for conditional κ = 1.5878574e-5 > 2^-16
body:
PR #29 charges all 107 data-corner pivots separately. Exact rank-partition identities expose two compatible, contiguous blocks of widths **51 and 45** in that same prescribed basis. Keeping its physical producers, topology, frames and paid endpoint correction gives

$$T(n)=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad \kappa=\frac{7939287}{500000000000}=1.5878574\times10^{-5}>2^{-16}.$$

This conditional exponent saving is **2.20503% above PR #29's 1.5536e-5 witness**. This compares asymptotic exponent savings, not practical runtimes.

### Geometric proof

At the retained dimensions (55,53), the 107-square null corner is diagonally equivalent to

$$M=F\,\operatorname{diag}(x_0,\ldots,x_{54},y_0,\ldots,y_{52},-1)\,G^T,$$

where F and G are the actual prescribed incidence matrices augmented by a constant column. The last-corner residue offset is **52**, and is explicitly retained.

For an augmented k-square minor, partition its coefficient columns into X and Y. The bound

$$\operatorname{rank}(U D V^T)\leq\operatorname{rank}(U_X)+\operatorname{rank}(V_Y)<k$$

proves an exact zero identity for every diagonal weight. The package supplies **2,265 such certificates**, verifies all **4,530 ranks with integer elimination**, and gives a normalized rational witness with all **107 ordered pivots nonzero**. These identities establish the required Schur zeros for all weights; the witness establishes nonvanishing on the actual normalized projector family. The written finite-product argument places the new conditions in PR29's same free GL55 × GL53 basis family.

An independent worker separately reconstructed every required augmented minor, checked every partition rank without the search oracle, reproduced the rational pivot sequence, and checked the physical order. The two runs occupy rows1..51/columns2863..2913 and rows58..102/columns2812..2856; the width2701 middle remains coordinates107..2807. No separated coordinates are gathered.

### Exact cost and assembly

The data profile changes from **107 singletons + 2701** to **11 singletons + 51 + 45 + 2701**, preserving rank2808. Across 2N data macros, the histogram removes 192N singleton calls and adds 2N calls of each new width. The paid N endpoint-copy corrections remain.

The original m=2915, W=31753659079 and rank sum=92561585391935 are unchanged. The exact bit saving becomes **15879079/10^12**. PR21's complex saving 18e-6, PR23's semantic C1=1 and PR29's beta=1/10 are retained. All **47 strict constraints and seven final margins** pass. The product row degree is recomputed and remains **47000**; no producer, routing, phase or bulk mechanism is newly claimed.

### Validation and scope

The written proof, exact coefficient certificates, rational witness, full histogram and final assembly are included with source provenance and negative controls. title: Add Gaussian parity proofs and mixed-center community integration
body:
This adds an exact arithmetic and precision integration for the community's actual mixed-center producer. Starting from arbitrary dirty scalar ports, subtracting old/new values before division and collecting the side corrections produces an integer-only reference decoder. The completed-child denominator certificate is then applied to the pinned 29-class PR46 profile. The result includes a paper, 168 Lean theorem declarations, executable interfaces, source-pinned audits, and provenance.

The new standalone package is [`research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/`](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/tree/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis). The earlier 69-theorem package in `research/gaussian-parity/` is retained unchanged.

Entry points: [paper PDF](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/community-parity-synthesis.pdf), [LaTeX source](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/community-parity-synthesis.tex), [reproduction/interface README](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/README.md), [formalization map](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/FORMALIZATION_MAP.md), [community ledger](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/LEDGER.md), and [provenance](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/PROVENANCE.md).

## Combined result

The source inventory covers all 46 PRs available at the start of this run, with pinned heads and 5,380 cumulative changed-file records, plus Swapnil Jain's separate Round 6 work. The concrete integration targets PR46 at `71b6c960c89295e952522dd44111df9cfc51ae90`, which retains the mixed-center/copied-center chain, changed-DAG and fixed-basis work, reversed geometry, PR44's weighted matching, and direct rational data recovery. These overlapping contributions are not treated as independently additive improvements. The inventory does not claim every community build was executed.

- **Exact dirty-port scalar decoder:** for the actual h28,d19 producer, `sum delta B - 2 sum delta D = -32 T`; the remaining collected numerators are `2 X`. The fused reference schedule needs zero additional fractional bits versus six in the explicitly compared generic old/new reference schedule. Gaussian quotient calls decrease from 26,268 to 3,286 in those schedules, excluding the optional image check and physical frame costs. These are reference-arithmetic counts, not measured runtime or optimality claims.
- **Complete image guard and usable adapter:** local divisibility is insufficient. `checked_fused_delta` checks `P(Q delta)==delta`, rejecting locally divisible off-image examples. `mixed_center_adapter.py` connects canonical, heterogeneous Gaussian tags to the actual integer producer/decoder at an explicitly promised common input grid. All center and side ports must share one phase frame; matching phases within individual roles is insufficient.
- **Actual-profile precision certificate:** the 29 complex child classes have old completed-child charge `421548223824*f`. Their certified charge is `(421548223824*f + 1142904672*(f mod 2))/2`, bounded by `211345564248*f` for every natural parallel width. This reduces that component by **49.864439629%**. Scalar E, global guard, unfinished recursion, tape/memory costs, normalized H0 output and the multiplication exponent are separately charged and unchanged by this certificate.
- **Formal tensor execution:** `GaussianTensorExecution.lean` defines and executes the full finite recursive C tensor in every dimension. It proves tagged forward/inverse restoration, the terminal `p+ceil(D/2)` binary grid, odd-depth parity and sharpness using an actually executed impulse. This closes the earlier written-only execution link for that finite tensor algorithm; it does not certify physical frame/tape compilation.

The mixed-center inverse identity and Gaussian parity principles are inherited mathematics. The contribution is their combined exact dirty-difference implementation, guarded concrete producer integration, all-dimensional finite tensor execution proof, and source-linked actual-profile accounting.

## Authorship and provenance

**Alejandro Zarzuelo Urdiales** is the author and human developer. This research began in an earlier **Archivara** exploration of parity-aware integer multiplication. Alejandro subsequently developed the line personally with multiple AI tools, most recently **GPT-6.1**, as recorded by the author. This synthesis, paper, Lean proofs, controls and submission preparation involved substantial **OpenAI Codex** assistance.

The earlier exploration supplies the parity motivation. The arithmetic used here has independent proofs; this submission does not inherit its broader separation, carry-saving or benchmark assertions.

The package credits OpenAI's pinned manuscript; Douglas Colkitt/CrocSwap; icekylinx; Zhihao Chen/jacklightChen; RaD/hipotures; Aurel Prosz/Paureel; James Chang/jamesyc; Dominik Scholz; Rohan Arun; Chafik Boukhalfa/chafreaky; Swapnil Jain; and the contributors and AI disclosures retained in the upstream NOTICE and complete ledger. Gaussian denominator exponents and parity reduction are established prior work in Amy, Glaudell and Ross, Quantum 4, 252 (2020), section 5.4. No priority claim is made for these inherited principles or identities. New material is Apache-2.0; vendored source retains its original LICENSE, NOTICE and exact bytes.

## Validation and limits

- Lean 4.31.0, bundled Std only: five proof modules and the complete 168-theorem axiom audit pass `lake build`; **99 theorem declarations are new** beyond the earlier package. Dependencies are standard Lean foundational axioms only, with no omitted proofs, project axioms or `native_decide`.
- Four standalone Python audits pass. The actual producer audit checks all **10,732,176 source/target coefficients** using exact integer bitplanes, six all-target dirty trials and negative image/frame controls. Two additional canonical-tag adapter trials exercise all 3,276 sources and 13,132 dirty ports with heterogeneous tags. The profile is checked against the full vendored pinned certificate before its arithmetic is used. Modified pinned source and optimized Python assertion execution are rejected.
- The phase/oracle controls include 729 canonical cases, 10,000 heterogeneous pairs, 15,000 operations and 10,752 exact phase-endpoint values. The all-width charge is a Lean theorem, supplemented by finite controls.
- The four-page PDF compiles with Tectonic and every rendered page was inspected. All staged artifact hashes match the included manifest.
- The original package's checks and 188 upstream unit tests passed in the earlier commit. The upstream full generator/integration `make verify` was **not** rerun for this addition.

The concrete finite producer link is independently checked by Python; Lean proves the generic image-interface contract and the finite recursive tensor, not a full Python refinement or physical network compiler. Analytic/recovery premises, fixed-tape schedules, full multiplication theorem, physical runtime and any new kappa remain outside the demonstrated result.

Reproduce offline with `cd research/gaussian-parity-synthesis && make verify`, or use `verify.ps1` with Lean 4.31.0 and Python 3.10+ on PATH. Vendored runtime dependencies and exact source hashes are included; no upstream checkout or third-party Python package is required.

title: Skip-prefix strips: conditional κ = 4498144/10^11 > 2^-15
body:
**κ = 4498144/10^11 ≈ 4.498144×10⁻⁵ > 2⁻¹⁵**, conditional on OpenAI's base theorem and the retained analytic and fixed-tape interfaces. That is **9.2146906% above #48** (411862541/10^13), which it builds on. It is also 7.8378235% above the highest open claim at the time of writing, #51 (4171211781/10^14); #49 and #50 claim 4.123863984e-5 and 4.129418696e-5. The exact bit saving is 4498347/10^11.

## Change and mathematical scope

This builds on #48 (`b7194b8`), so the branch also carries the #43, #46 and #48 commits; only the last commit is new. Everything except the scalar producer is #48's `research/copied-fixed` pipeline, with constants recomputed. The new files are in `research/skip-strips/`.

**What changes.** Every vertex's leave-one-out strip sums use a **skip-prefix** layout:

`s_j = A_{j−2} + (v_{j−1} + B_{j+1})` instead of `s_j = A_{j−1} + B_{j+1}`

In the ordinary layout, the two consumers of each prefix A_i are A_{i+1} and s_{i+1}. Their envelopes are incomparable, so the second use always costs a fresh role. With the skip layout, the consumers of A_i are A_{i+1} and s_{i+2}, and cover(A_{i+1}) ⊆ cover(s_{i+2}). Likewise, the new node v_{i−1} + B_{i+1} sits inside B_{i−1}. The inherited carrier matching can join these nested pairs.

- **Layout details.** The top level runs the layout on the reversed value list. Deeper levels run it on values sorted by (support size, ±support), #48's idea. Totals follow #48's rules.
- **Matching.** It is #44's weighted optimizer, pinned in `links-{23,25}.uses` and regenerable with `optimize_matching.py`.

| | #48 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| additions (h=23 / 25) | 37,098 / 49,119 | 40,329 / 53,475 |
| carrier links (h=23 / 25) | 6,002 / 7,715 | 12,719 / 16,991 |
| roles R (h=23 / 25) | 36,432 / 48,329 | 32,946 / 43,409 |
| physical wires W | 177,530,859 | 160,799,739 |

**Hypotheses.** No hypothesis or interface changes; the bound uses the same inherited framework as #48. Two points of scope:
- This result leans more heavily on the carrier-continuation rule than #48 does. Without carrier matching, the new DAG has more roles than #48's (45,665 vs 42,434 at h=23).
- #40 and later, including #48, are outside the maintainer audit of #39 (`docs/research/community-final-audit.md`). This PR inherits that status.

## Validation

**Finite checks.** `make skip-strips-verify` checks:
- scalar exactness: every output is the exact leave-two-out sum or retained total;
- the original-envelope labels;
- pinned-link legality: every link is replayed in `profiles.cpp` and recounted independently;
- the fixed I+J profiles: 61,461 / 82,606 distinct transition matrices, 5,642 / 7,434 of them checked under several primes (CRT), with 0 disagreements;
- the full physical timeline and every dirty-scratch basis vector, in both orientations;
- all 4,073,300 data pairs, with exact rational recovery of the ten primary-prime failures;
- the exact moment, plus exact lower bounds showing that the #36 baseline and the #40–#44 and #46–#48 networks fail at the new bit saving;
- all 47 strict assembly conditions and 7 margins.

`tests/test_skip_strips.py` adds 20 tests, including leave-one-out exactness, the cover-nesting identity and negative controls.

An earlier version of the same change, applied on top of #43, was audited independently from clean copies. The audit re-ran the full producer check and recomputed every transition profile in exact rational arithmetic, with no modular step. It found no correctness issue. The stacked version here has not had that separate audit.

**Proof arguments.** As in #41, #47 and #48, which also changed the producer DAG, the new DAG enters the inherited proofs only through properties and quantities that the finite checks above recompute: disjoint additions, common points, exact outputs, admissible carrier links, the physical timeline and the transition profiles. The cover-nesting identity explains why the matching finds more links; correctness does not depend on it. The inherited written obligations are not re-proved here: the base theorem, the residual compiler and fixed-tape recursion, the physical meaning of carrier continuations and copied centers, and the analytic, routing and eventual-threshold interfaces. This is not a formal verification, and no global optimality or speedup is claimed.

title: Dual suffix-skip strips: conditional κ = 4541011/10^11 > 2^-15
body:
## Summary

We introduce the mathematical dual **skip-suffix** layout for leave-one-out strip sums in the 2D $(23, 25)$ data-corner geometry:

$$s_j = (A_{j-1} + v_{j+1}) + B_{j+2}$$

This improves the certified exponent bound to:

$$T(n) = O\bigl(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\bigr), \qquad \boxed{\kappa = \frac{4541011}{10^{11}} = 4.541011 \times 10^{-5} > 2^{-15}}$$

This bound **cleanly beats PR #54** ($141532521/3125000000000 = 4.529040672 \times 10^{-5}$) without checking in 250,000 lines of paid-clone tables, beats **PR #53** ($4498144/10^{11} = 4.498144 \times 10^{-5}$) by **+0.953%**, and beats **PR #48** ($411862541/10^{13}$) by **+10.255%**.

---

## Architectural Duality vs PR #53 (Skip-Prefix)

In PR #53, the leave-one-out strips were computed via the skip-prefix layout $s_j = A_{j-2} + (v_{j-1} + B_{j+1})$. While this nested prefix consumers, it introduced a structural asymmetry: pairing small-support leaves with large-support suffix sums collapsed core popcounts ($	ext{core} \to 1$). Consequently, `SharedPointCircuit` failed to merge additions across common-point groups.

By contrast, the dual **skip-suffix** layout:
- Groups additions into intermediate sums $A_{j-1} + v_{j+1}$ that maintain compact cover envelopes and core popcounts $\ge 2$.
- Enables `SharedPointCircuit` to merge **530+ additions** across groups.
- Expands carrier matching capacity by **+175 matches** on $h=23$ and **+60 matches** on $h=25$.

### Full Circuit Comparison

| **Total Wires ($W$)** | 177,530,859 | 160,799,739 | 159,592,676 | **159,230,679** | **-361,997** |
| **Bit Saving ($a_\text{bit}$)** | $4.118833 \times 10^{-5}$ | $4.498347 \times 10^{-5}$ | $4.529240 \times 10^{-5}$ | **$4.541218 \times 10^{-5}$** | **+$1.198 \times 10^{-7}$** |
| **Certified $\kappa$** | $4.118625 \times 10^{-5}$ | $4.498144 \times 10^{-5}$ | $4.529040 \times 10^{-5}$ | **$4.541011 \times 10^{-5}$** | **+$1.197 \times 10^{-7}$** |
| **External Clone Tables** | None | None | 251,571 lines JSON | **None (Pure Algebraic)** | **-251.5k lines** |

---

## Hardware Verification & Controls

All results are certified on hardware through the standard repository pipeline:
1. `c.verify()`: Passed cancellation-free and leave-two-out output equivalence on both axes.
2. `dense_audit(c)`: Passed exact global bitset support containment.
3. `profiles.cpp` (across 3 Mersenne primes $2^{61}-1, 2^{31}-1, 524287$):
   - $h=23$: 5,379 CRT matrices checked, **0 modular disagreements**.
   - $h=25$: 7,179 CRT matrices checked, **0 modular disagreements**.
4. `original_timeline.py`: Checked all $32,541$ roles on $h=23$ and $43,049$ roles on $h=25$ in both orientations without dirty vector discrepancies.
5. `data_corners.cpp`: Full replay of all 4,073,300 data pairs with exact rational recovery of the 10 primary-prime fallbacks (accelerated via OpenMP to under 10 seconds).
6. Moment certificate: $a_\text{bit} = \frac{4541218}{10^{11}}$ upper bound $0.99999999999988 < 1$ with strict gap $1.208 \times 10^{-13}$. The next grid point $4541219/10^{11}$ strictly fails with lower bound $1.00000000000432 > 1$.

The new conditional witness is

The interval/core-aware scalar graph and fixed I+J rational basis are retained. The compiler now prices complete retired dependency circuits using actual transition child profiles, including provider promotions and deferred cleanup. It then uses bounded moment-improving carried-signal exchanges under the existing linear-independence and distinct-use constraints: **670 exchanges on h23 and 825 on h25**. These are heuristic local improvements; no weighted matroid optimum is claimed.

The cost objective comes from our exact complete-characteristic feasibility framework, rather than selecting solely by wire count or primitive XOR count. Rank-flow identities prove why subtracting linear rank preserves local price order at fixed cardinality. Universal dirty-word proofs ensure that changing the legal encoder/complement preserves arbitrary dirty scratch when the separate fresh-transfer contract is maintained.

title: Searched orders on PR #49's graphs: conditional κ = 4.125007391e-5
body:
## Summary

A complete single-bit-flip descent over PR #49's pinned adjacent-swap orders,
with the **role count** as the objective rather than the number of matched
carriers.

PR #49 pinned a greedy climb over the `total()` / `vector()` order bits and its
scope note explicitly disclaims global optimality. Two things differ here:

1. **The objective.** A flip can add matched carriers *and* add more additions at
   the same time, so maximising carriers is not the same as minimising
   `R = c + q - matched`. Since `W = 2N + sum_h (N // v_h) * R_h` holds the child
   list fixed, `R` is what moves the role volume and hence the exponent, so the
   descent minimises `R` directly (matched carriers and log-weight as
   tie-breaks).
2. **The search.** Every decision bit (1584 at h=23, 1900 at h=25) is flipped and
   evaluated end to end; the best strict improvement is accepted and the pass
   repeats until no single flip improves — instead of one greedy sweep.

| | PR #49 | This |
|---|---:|---:|
| h=23 roles R (matched) | 36,382 (6,077) | **36,341 (6,153)** |
| h=25 roles R (matched) | 48,255 (7,809) | **48,247 (7,825)** |
| Width W | 177,284,805 | **177,176,337** |
| bit saving | 4124034054/10^14 | **825035511/2·10^13** |
| **kappa** | 4123863984/10^14 | **4125007391/10^14** |

**+0.02773%**, still above `2^-15`. Everything else is PR #48/#49 unchanged:
RaD's point order and original-envelope labels, both fixed I+J bases, copied
centers, paid endpoint corrections, reversed data corners with exact recovery of
all ten fallbacks, the complex layer and the balanced assembly.

## Verification

Run with the repository's own machinery on this branch:

- `make ordered-descent-check` → `witness.py` derives the bit saving and kappa
  from the searched rows and certified profiles by grid search (not pinned
  constants) and checks the 47 assembly constraints, the seven margins, the
  rejection of the next bit and kappa grid points, and the exclusion of **nine**
  earlier networks at the new saving — including PR #49's own — plus six focused
  tests.
- `make ordered-descent-producer` → `producer.py` replays both dimensions with
  PR #43's independent checkers imported unchanged: scalar identity, dense
  global-bitset audit, the pinned matching read back by `profiles.cpp` with every
  edge asserted admissible, an independent recount of every matched use, and the
  complete physical timeline and dirty basis in both orientations. CRT
  disagreements are zero. The replay reproduces the stored artifacts
  byte-for-byte on a second run.
- The graphs are rebuilt from the committed bit vectors on every run, so
  `bits-{23,25}.json` plus the committed rows/profiles/matchings are the whole
  input.

Cross-checks performed while building this: the two-stage matcher used here is an
instrumented build of the pinned `scripts/partial_swap/match_positive_dag.cpp`
(the file is unchanged between this branch and PR #49), and upstream's own
`profiles.cpp` with its own Hopcroft–Karp independently reports the same
`matched` and `R` for every graph used here.

## Scope and limits — please read before merging

- This is a **single-bit local optimum** of the order space, not a global one,
  and no global optimality of the matcher is claimed beyond the pinned max-weight
  maximum matchings.
- The descent was **still finding improvements when it was stopped** (`R` had
  reached 36,336 and 48,239 in the unfinished next passes), so the reported
  numbers are a lower bound on what this search reaches.
- The search harness itself (bit-vector descent with the role-count objective) is
  not shipped; the searched bit vectors, rows, certified profiles, matchings,
  witness and certificate are.
- The inherited PR #48 dependencies and the analytic hypotheses are unchanged and
  remain conditional.

If you prefer, I can split the docs/README-headline change out, or hold the
headline at PR #49 until you have reviewed the witness.

## Files

- `research/ordered-descent/README.md` — result, method, checks, limits
- `research/ordered-descent/{bits,original,profiles,scalar,timeline}-{23,25}.json`,
  `links-{23,25}.uses` — searched inputs and replayed artifacts
- `research/ordered-descent/{witness,producer}.py`, `climbed_graph.py`,
  `optimize_matching.py`, `profiles.cpp`, `certificate.json`, `SOURCE.json`
- `tests/test_ordered_descent.py`; `Makefile` (`ordered-descent-verify` wired into
  `verify-community`); root `README.md` exponent updated

## Attribution

Base graphs, orders, matching objective and composition: **Chafik Boukhalfa**
(PR #48) and **Rohan Arun** (PR #49, with Anthropic Claude assistance), building
on RaD / hipotures (PR #41), icekylinx, James Chang, Dominik Scholz, Zhihao Chen,
Aurel Prosz / Paureel, Swapnil Jain, eumemic, Douglas Colkitt, OpenAI and
Harvey–van der Hoeven. The searched-order descent, the role-count objective and
this run were produced with AI assistance (Codebuff/Claude).

This PR certifies a new finite conditional witness $\kappa = \frac{52431959054651}{10^{18}} = 5.2431959054651 \times 10^{-5}$ for integer multiplication, improving upon PR #84 ($\kappa = 5.22712890914 \times 10^{-5}$) by $+0.307377\%$, as well as subsequent refinements (PR #85 and PR #86).

### Key Architectural Advance

1. **Congruent Balanced Multi-Splits `[4, 4, 1]`:**
   - Previous indexed-cycle architectures applied multi-split code `4` (splitting both `first` and `mid` pairs) asymmetrically (`[4, 1, 1]` on $h=23$; `[1, 4, 1]` on $h=25$).
   - Applying `[4, 4, 1]` congruently across both axes contracts eligible pairs across two consecutive recursion depths while satisfying the strict contraction guard $\text{groups} + \text{splits} + 1 < \text{points}$.
   - **Role contractions:**
     - $h=23$: $26,834 \to \mathbf{26,705}$ ($-129$ roles; rank mass $617,688 \to 614,721$).
     - $h=25$: $35,348 \to \mathbf{35,137}$ ($-211$ roles; rank mass $884,300 \to 879,025$).
   - **Physical width $W$:** Compacted from $132,466,108 \to \mathbf{131,795,727}$ ($-670,381$ bit coordinates).

2. **Dirty-Basis Replay and CRT Profiles:**
   - Serialized physical words generated with `dirty=True` in both forward and dual orientations.
   - Replayed all $2v + R$ basis vectors: PASS.
   - Reconstructed exact frame transitions directly from literal XORs: PASS.
   - Profiled via C++ oracle over Mersenne prime $p = 2^{61}-1$: 0 CRT modular disagreements on both axes ($5,535$ matrices on $h=23$, $7,334$ matrices on $h=25$).

3. **Certified Recurrence & Assembly Bounds:**
   - Certified bit saving: $a_{\text{bit}} = \frac{6554338538661}{125000000000000} = \frac{52434708309288}{10^{18}} \approx 5.2434708309288 \times 10^{-5}$.
   - Moment enclosure: $M(s) < 1$ and $M(s + 10^{-18}) > 1$ under directed Taylor8 and independent 60-term degree-12 $\mathrm{atanh}$ expansions.
   - Certified conditional exponent: $\kappa = \frac{52431959054651}{10^{18}} = 5.2431959054651 \times 10^{-5}$.
   - All 47 strict assembly inequalities $> 0$, all 7 safety margins $> \kappa$.
   - Historical profiles of PR #74, PR #79, and PR #84 are strictly excluded ($M_{\text{old}}(s) > 1$).

4. **Pipeline & Makefile Parallelization:**
   - Makefile updated to run all verifier audits, tests, and core verification concurrently with `-j32`.
   - Core verifier runs $h=23$ and $h=25$ concurrently via `ProcessPoolExecutor`.

### Verification

```sh
make indexed-cycle-verify
```
All audits, unit tests, and full dirty-basis replays pass with exit code 0 across 32 threads.

title: Certify ordered-frame composition at κ = 5.2514124198891e-5
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This composes rank-preserving envelope ties, coordinate-aware oracle prices and bounded three-donor carrier exchanges with the complete indexed construction from #84:

**κ = 52514124198891/1000000000000000000 = 5.2514124198891e-5**, with bit saving **52516882077117/1000000000000000000**.

The exact value is **0.4645669003% above the pinned #84 construction** `88ca39571907343a49e97f328971ec7bcd26fbfd`. Complete #84 and reported pinned #74 paid recursive profiles are strictly excluded at the new accepted bit saving. This also exceeds the reported #85 value 5.2272192668365e-5 (`fb1f2c57681cd7c0b86a192de9367a7af87c9cca`) and #86 value 5.2275423755251e-5 (`d1b2a3a7caec9a101363e5c534a4680a1d2086ba`), observed 2026-10-08. These are historical reported-head comparisons; the actual pricing source is #82. No foreign producer replay or current-global-frontier claim is implied. A later #74 update (`428b5c167686b42a83f1abf7003c6d17aec561ea`) reports κ=5.278214423139e-5, above this frozen witness; it does not change the historical comparison or numerical certificate here.

The result remains a finite conditional witness under the inherited ordered residual compiler, all-size recursion, finite scalar overhead, routing, prime selection, exact recovery, fixed-tape and analytic transfer interfaces. It is not an unconditional or fully formal multiplication theorem, a global optimum or a practical speed benchmark. The complete original #84 construction and all earlier source and finite evidence remain preserved.

### Construction

| Selected choice | h23 | h25 |
|---|---|---|
| Recursive split vector | `[4,4,4]` | `[4,4,1]` |
| Rank-first envelope ties | descending cover, then core | original PR74 |
| Output routing | baseline | descending future-use deadline |
| Oracle coordinate pricing | identity | final selected coordinates |
| Three-donor passes / accepted cycles | 0 / 0 | at most 3 / 2 |
| Auxiliary roles | 26,581 | 35,133 |

Both axes retain anchored point order, balanced half-plane coarse sums, future-compatible unit completion, exact retired/pending indexes, pending next-use scoring and bounded single/two-cycle exchanges. Both use explicit coordinate maps selected by our bounded R6 search. The full width is **131,503,443**; recursive rank is **75,612,632,825**; rank deficit is **1,846,900**; largest child/parent dimension is **529/575**. Bit wire bits and row coefficient remain **27/843**.

Distinct scalar envelopes strictly increase cover-size minus core-size along an edge, so rank-first ordering preserves dependencies while retaining original order inside each envelope. Pricing changes only serialized heuristic masks, leaving legality checks and in-memory frames untouched. Three-donor cycles independently check each final local basis and preserve distinct future-use ownership and cardinality while strictly decreasing a fixed integer score. Final profiles are freshly recomputed; all XORs, frame raises, copies, centers, dirty inputs, endpoints and cleanup remain charged.

All earlier contributor, OpenAI, manuscript, license and AI-assistance notices remain attached. The 590-file original #84 construction closure, immutable 90-pin final discovery runtime and original #82 inputs remain in separate hash-checked archives.

title: Scheduled region orders on balanced frames: conditional κ = 5.2111890493145e-5
body:
## Dependency

This branch is composed on top of the open #82 head (`3410b94`), so its diff against `main` includes that PR's content, exactly as #82 itself composes the pinned PR76/PR79 archive. The candidate added by this PR is the fourteen files under `research/envelope-scheduled/` plus `.github/workflows/envelope-scheduled.yml`.

## What this composes

The pinned envelope-balanced witness fixes one region order per axis through
`balanced_split_graph.configuration(h)['schedule']` (`cover-core` at h23,
`reverse-node` at h25). This candidate keeps every other setting — groups
`[1,1,2]`, anchors, half-plane versus row coarse sums, future-compatible
completion, 0 versus 3 carry-exchange passes, exact next-use profile costs, the
coordinate-conjugated oracle pricing at h25, the PR74 scalar-envelope
reordering, and the pinned coordinate orders `order-23.json` / `order-25.json`
— and changes only the region order: `node-asc` at h23, `width-node` at h25.

## Result

| Quantity | Pinned witness | This candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| kappa (1e-18 grid) | 5.2032798885190e-05 | **5.2111890493145e-05** |
| Bit saving | 5.2035506438388e-05 | 5.2114606283958e-05 |
| h23 / h25 auxiliary roles | 27075 / 35500 | 27032 / 35431 |
| Physical width W | 133289600 | 133068501 |

kappa = 10422378098629/200000000000000000, which is 15818321591/200000000000000000
absolute (**+0.152%**) above the pinned 5203279888519/100000000000000000, and
+0.72% above PR76's 5.1738676045141e-05. The improvement also survives on the
coarser 1e-11 grid (5.211188e-05, still above the pinned fine-grid value).

The candidate is *narrower* than the pin and has *fewer* auxiliary roles, so
this is not a width effect: the region order changes which rank-one blocks the
profiler extracts from the same physical path, and the moment inequality
`sum_t count_t (t/m)^(1-s) / W < 1` is decided by that profile shape.

## How the orders were selected

Region orders were scored by recompiling axes and evaluating the unchanged
exact arithmetic: 12 h23 orders (9 keys plus 4 hash-seeded random orders, with
`cover-core` reproducing the pinned axis-23 word byte for byte) crossed with 10
h25 orders, 120 pairs in total, at 8-20 minutes of compilation per axis. The
best pair is `node-asc` with `width-node`; at h25 the `node-asc` and
`width-node` keys happen to produce the same order.

Coordinate relabelling was searched separately as an independent lever: more
than 500 hill-climbing and random relabel draws on the pinned words never beat
the identity relabel, so the pinned `order-23.json` and `order-25.json` are
retained unchanged. Only the region order moved the number.

## What is verified

`research/envelope-scheduled/verify.py` replays both words (XOR word, dirty
basis, frame incidence), rebuilds the transition and fixed-basis profile
receipts, recomputes the profile of each axis exactly against the shipped
`profiles-23.json` / `profiles-25.json`, rebuilds the complete
child-multiplicity profile, re-derives the 1e-18 grid saving with the inherited
rational binary search, checks both moment enclosures, the independent
log-enclosure audit bound, the fixed-width bridge and the balanced assembly,
and asserts all 47 strict inequalities, the seven margins, the next-grid kappa
rejection and the independent-bound separation. `--regenerate` recompiles both
axes through this directory's `compiler.py` (role counts 27032 and 35431) and
asserts the regenerated words are byte-identical to the shipped ones; the
recorded run is `regen.log`. `test_controls.py` adds 15 controls: a duplicated
coordinate, an inconsistent mapping, unrelabelled source values or outputs, a
missing terminal synthesis, an aliased terminal, an unknown region order, a
region order that breaks the topological or carrier constraints, and a stale
bridge field are all rejected, while the recorded kappa is accepted and its
next 1e-18 grid value is rejected. CI runs both in the same three Python
versions as the pinned workflow.

## Scope and limits

The arithmetic downstream of the words is inherited unchanged: the PR48
rational logarithm enclosures, the PR65 moment/assembly/audit code, the
fixed-tape transfer, routing and recovery interfaces, prime selection and the
all-size compiler argument. Only heuristic selection among legal region orders
changed, under the same topological and carrier-candidate assertions. Nothing
in `research/envelope-balanced/` is modified; `compiler.py` and
`flag_engine.py` are copies of the pinned files in this directory, and the
copied flag engine keeps the pinned `check_flag_engine` assertion. The one
harness difference is that the oracle subprocess is awaited with a generous
timeout instead of ten seconds, because the pinned ten-second wait aborts an
already *completed* compilation at its shutdown step under parallel load,
before the word is written; it cannot change the word, which is fully
determined before that step.

This remains a conditional finite witness: no global optimality over region
orders and no measured practical speedup is claimed.

Region-order selection and verification with Codebuff (Buffy) assistance.
Inherited sources, notices and licenses remain unchanged.
